title: AI based Virtual Yoga Instructor for Good health
summary: C-DAC Pune reports that its AI-based Virtual Yoga Instructor, a MoveNet-based pose classifier, identified ten yoga poses with an accuracy of 0.86 on test data; no practitioner result is reported.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: The Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) in Pune built a virtual instructor that uses AI to recognize yoga poses and give feedback. The C-DAC team described the system in a paper at the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Kaleidoscope conference in New Delhi in October 2024. The authors report that their MoveNet-based classifier identified ten yoga poses with an accuracy of 0.86 on test data. They report no trial with practitioners. In its 2025 entry in an ITU report, C-DAC lists an active demonstration and plans a wider pose dataset and a mobile application. Its proposed benefits include accessible exercise guidance and preventive health education. No source reports a fitness or health improvement for any practitioner.
purpose: Make yoga instruction and posture feedback more accessible.
developer: Centre for Development of Advanced Computing, Pune
